task.description: Rework 2 of 3 for ISS-0427 design, per CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's rework-1 re-gate FAIL (handoffs/WF03-ISS0427-20260904/step-02b-code-design-validator-regate.json). One MAJOR: column types from a custom Postgres DOMAIN or ENUM stay schema-qualified to the template after LIKE INCLUDING ALL, uncovered by any of the 12 dimensions or open questions -- root cause traced to information_schema.columns (the design's own instrument) resolving domain/enum columns down to their base type by SQL-standard spec, structurally unable to see this class of divergence. Required beyond the fix itself: re-examine every information_schema use in the design against pg_catalog ground truth for the same blind-spot shape, not just patch the one found instance. Two MINORs: index comments uncovered by dimension #8 (dormancy unconfirmed by the validator), and a missing '## 1.' header orphaned by rework 1's edit, breaking section 11's cross-reference.

result.summary:
lib/letflow/design/iss0427-tenant-test-schema-template-clone.md updated in place. New section 0.3 documents the rework-2 findings and the information_schema-vs-pg_catalog re-examination the coordinator specifically asked for.

MAJOR, independently re-verified: built probe_tpl.positive_int (a DOMAIN) and probe_tpl.color_enum (a plain ENUM), used both as column types on a template table, cloned via LIKE INCLUDING ALL. pg_attribute+pg_type ground truth confirmed the clone's columns have the TEMPLATE's own type objects, not clone-local ones; pg_depend confirmed a real (deptype='n') dependency from the clone's column to the template's type. Reproduced the corruption cascade too: dropping probe_tpl before probe_clone cascaded into and destroyed the clone's own columns (same failure the validator demonstrated); dropping clone-then-template was clean. All probe schemas dropped and confirmed gone (SELECT nspname FROM pg_namespace WHERE nspname LIKE 'probe%' OR nspname='tenant_template' -- 0 rows) both after this round and after the earlier collation-focused probe round.

ROOT-CAUSE RE-EXAMINATION (the part the coordinator said mattered most): walked all four information_schema uses in the design against pg_catalog ground truth, not just the one the validator found. information_schema.tables (dimension #1, table-name set): NOT a gap -- a table's own identity IS its own schema+name, no indirection to hide, confirmed directly against pg_class. information_schema.columns.collation_name (dimension #6, originally in the Collations sub-bullet): A SECOND REAL GAP, found by this same re-examination, same shape as the MAJOR -- built a genuinely custom collation (CREATE COLLATION ... provider=icu), used it on a template column, cloned it; information_schema.columns DOES carry a collation_schema field (separate from the bare collation_name the design actually compared) that correctly shows the clone's collation is still template-qualified, confirmed independently via pg_attribute.attcollation -> pg_collation.collnamespace. The original claim in that sub-bullet ('Postgres copies column collation under plain LIKE already ... expected-equal by construction') was corrected -- it was only true for the pg_catalog-owned default collation, not custom ones. information_schema.role_table_grants (item 8 Privileges rule-out): NOT a gap -- verified pg_class.relacl is empty on both sides directly; a privilege is a property of the (role,relation) pair itself, not a reference to a shared object another schema could still own, so there is no analogous indirection to miss. Stated explicitly: nowhere else in the design relies on an information_schema view for a property that could reference a shared, schema-qualified object outside the table/column being described -- every other dimension (#3,4,5,9,10,11) was already built directly against pg_catalog, never through an information_schema intermediary, so none of those was at risk of this failure mode.

FIX: new dimension #13 (column type and collation NAMESPACE) added to section 3.2 -- resolves the column's true type via pg_attribute.atttypid -> pg_type.typnamespace and true collation via pg_attribute.attcollation -> pg_collation.collnamespace, asserting a non-pg_catalog-owned type/collation's namespace on the candidate side equals the candidate's OWN schema, never the reference's -- the same structural, namespace-based (not name/string-based) discipline already used for indexes (dimension #4) and sequences (dimension #5). Currently a defaults-only assertion per the same soundness class the validator already accepted for dimensions #9-#11 (confirmed via grep: zero CREATE TYPE/CREATE DOMAIN/CREATE COLLATION anywhere in priv/repo/migrations/ today). Collations sub-bullet in dimension #8 corrected in place (not just left standing) to state plainly that bare collation_name comparison alone does not cover this and point to #13. WHAT THE MECHANISM DOES ABOUT IT, stated plainly as instructed: nothing today, correctly -- no domain/enum/collation object exists to recreate; slots into the existing OQ-2/OQ-5 pattern as new OQ-6, which spells out the future mechanism step (create a clone-local DOMAIN/TYPE/COLLATION from the template's own definition and repoint the column) symmetric to the FK-readd and sequence-recreation steps, not designed in full since nothing exists today to design a concrete step against.

MINOR 1 (index comments): confirmed the divergence directly (COMMENT ON INDEX does not survive LIKE INCLUDING ALL; COMMENT ON CONSTRAINT does, checked as a control). Confirmed FULL dormancy this rework, which the validator's own gate had left unconfirmed: grep -rl "COMMENT ON" priv/repo/migrations/*.exs returns zero hits of any kind (table/column/index/constraint) across every migration. Decision: ruled out with a stated reason (cosmetic only, no query/constraint/planner behavior depends on comment text, confirmed-zero dormancy), added explicitly as a sub-bullet under dimension #8 rather than silently absent -- same treatment already given to RLS/partitioning/tablespace (dimension #12).

MINOR 2 (missing header): restored '## 1. Scope and non-goals' above the orphaned In-scope/Out-of-scope content that rework 1's §0.2 insertion had left headerless. Verified no content was lost (read the orphaned text in place before restoring the header). Section 11's '§1 non-goals' cross-reference now resolves -- confirmed via grep that every ## N. header 0 through 11 is present and in order.

Dimension count: 12 -> 13. Both section 3.2's intro sentence and both section 3.4 use-site dimension ranges (build-time self-check: #1-6 and #8-#13 excluding #7; permanent regression test: all #1-13) updated accordingly.

Everything the re-gate confirmed as already correct (contype six-kind enumeration, reloptions dimension #9, attstattarget dimension #10, pg_statistic_ext dimension #11, the zero-vs-zero soundness class, dimension #12's explicit-non-active status, FK rewrite, sequence recreation, scope/production-path reachability, OQ-1, the speedup claim) was left untouched -- not re-litigated, per the coordinator's explicit instruction.

No implementation code added -- verified by grep for elixir/ex fenced code blocks after all edits (none found). No lib/ or test/ file touched by this rework, only the design doc. This handoff file's existence on disk was verified via a follow-up ls after writing it, per the coordinator's explicit instruction to verify before reporting back.
